what_happened: On a multi-lane freeway, with the command STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy's plan (orange) veered left toward actor 15, while the recorded human path (green) went straight and then right. The ego drifted into the lane on its left and its front hit actor 56, which was driving alongside there, at 7.2 s.

The ego was going straight in its highway lane at a steady ~8 m/s. Actor 33 came up from behind in the lane to the left, passed the ego and cut in across the lane line just ahead of it, and the ego's front clipped 33's rear-right corner at 6.6s. The camera smear at impact is 33 right beside the ego, not a cause.

On a multi-lane highway, after the policy took over, the ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.5 m/s and drifted left out of its lane, following a planned path toward actor 15's lane, while the recorded route went straight and then right. Its front hit actor 56, which was driving alongside in the lane to its left.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy planned and carried out a left lane change while speeding up from 4.4 to 6.5 m/s. It cut into the adjacent left lane right where vehicle 56 was alongside, just ahead and to the left. The ego's front hit 56 at 7.2 s. The camera smear at impact came from being that close to 56 and did not cause the mistake.

The ego held its lane at about 8 m/s, heading slightly right with the route command. Actor 33 came up from behind on the left and passed close alongside, then cut toward the ego's lane and clipped its front-left corner at 6.6 s. The recorded human driver had moved left into that lane instead, so the replayed actor wasn't reacting to where the ego actually was.

The ego was cruising straight on a multi-lane highway at about 8 m/s with a large gap ahead (over 25 m). Actor 33, a replayed car in the lane to the left and behind it, came up and overtook it on the left. At 6.6 s it was alongside and overlapping the ego's front-left corner. The ego was only 0.9 m off the recorded path, drifting slightly left and straddling the lane line, which the human driver also crossed. The contact is a sideswipe from a replayed car overtaking it, not a failure to brake for a car ahead, and the run is also marked rear_ended.

Actor 9 came up from behind in the ego's lane and hit its rear at about 3.7s, while the ego was still replaying the recorded drive. By 4.7s, when the policy took over, actor 9 had driven up onto the ego's box and was registered as a front collision. The ego was exactly on the recorded path (0.0 m off) and had no time to react, so this looks like a log-replay actor overlapping the ego, not a mistake by the policy.

At 3.7s, actor 16 was just behind the ego in the same lane. By 4.7s it had driven forward into the ego's box, so the overlap was scored as a front collision. This happened at the handoff moment, while the ego was still exactly on the recorded human path (0.0 m off) and slowing slightly to 13.7 m/s, so the policy had no chance to react.

The ego was replaying the recorded drive, going straight at about 14 m/s with nothing ahead. Actor 16, a faster vehicle coming up from directly behind in the same lane, drove into and through the ego's box; at 4.7 s it overlaps the ego's front half. That registered as a front collision at the exact moment of handoff (4.7 s), before the policy had any chance to act, and the camera smear in that frame comes from the actor sitting inside the ego.

At 3.7s, actor 16 was directly behind the ego in the same lane. By 4.7s it had moved up and overlapped the ego's front, which was scored as a front collision. The ego was still exactly on the recorded human path (0.0 m off) at about 14 m/s, and the policy only took over at 4.7s, so this is a replayed actor driving through the ego, not a policy error.

The ego was still replaying the recorded trajectory (0.0 m off it, about 14 m/s, going straight) when actor 16 came up from directly behind in the same lane and drove through the ego's box. By 4.7 s it overlapped the ego's front half, so the collision was counted as a front collision. This happened at the handoff moment itself (4.7 s), so the policy never had control and could not have avoided it. The camera smear in the last frame is from the overlap at impact.

The ego was on the replayed human trajectory, 0.0 m off, at about 5 m/s on a straight highway lane with no car close ahead. Actor 9 came up from behind, hit the ego's rear by 3.7 s, and by 4.7 s its box covered the ego's, which the metrics also counted as a front collision. That 4.7 s mark is the instant the policy took over, so it had no chance to act.

Actor 9 came up from behind in the ego's lane, rear-ended the ego by 3.7 s and kept going until its box sat on top of the ego. That overlap is what registered as a front collision at 4.7 s, the moment the policy took over. Before that the ego was replaying the recorded drive (0 m off the recording) at a steady 5.6 m/s, with no vehicle ahead closer than about 40 m.

The ego was still replaying the recorded drive, straight in its lane at about 5 m/s (0.0 m off the recording). Actor 9 came up from behind, hit the ego's rear at 3.7 s, and kept driving into it until at 4.7 s it overlapped the whole ego box, which the metrics then count as a front collision at the same moment the policy took over.
